Question: Describe fleet-management dashboards where a single human oversees 10-50 agent instances: real-time status, health, progress, exception alerts; filterable by client, workflow type, risk, SLA.
Response: The Custom Control Plane UI is a purpose-built React application designed specifically for the 1:20-50 human-to-agent ratio WPP requires. The Fleet Manager agent composes the dashboard view: real-time workflow status (active, waiting, exception, completed), fleet health assessment, SLA tracking, and exception alerts. Filterable by: agency, market, jurisdiction, client, workflow type, risk level, SLA status. The default view is the Fleet Manager's intelligent assessment — not raw telemetry. Operators see a prioritised summary of their fleet. Drill-down: click any workflow for instant situational awareness. Data sources: Application Insights APIs (traces, token usage, cost), Foundry REST APIs (agent inventory), APIM metrics (token consumption, rate limit status), workflow state store (Cosmos DB/Dataverse — phase status, approvals, action ledger), Fleet Manager assessments (real-time via SignalR). The dashboard updates in real-time — no polling, no refresh needed.
Key Technologies: Custom Control Plane UI (React), Fleet Manager agent, SignalR (real-time), Application Insights, APIM metrics
POC Demo: POC1: Live fleet dashboard — Finance Controller managing 30-50 concurrent invoice workflows. Filterable, real-time, exception-driven. POC2: HR BP managing 15-20 hiring workflows across agencies and markets.

Question: How does the platform ensure humans see only the 2% needing attention? Describe intelligent filtering ranked by business impact and false-positive management.
Response: Exception-only surfacing is the Fleet Manager agent's primary function. The Fleet Manager consumes telemetry from all workflows and reasons about which require human attention. Filtering logic: (1) Confidence-based — workflows where the MAF agent executor's confidence was above the autonomy threshold (enforced by a downstream MAF validator executor via deterministic routing) proceed silently. Only below-threshold decisions surface. (2) Business impact ranking — exceptions are ranked by invoice value, candidate seniority, client priority, SLA urgency. High-impact exceptions surface first. (3) Pattern grouping — similar exceptions are batched for bulk approval (8 routine interview schedules, all low-risk). (4) False-positive management — when an operator dismisses an exception as unnecessary, the Fleet Manager logs the dismissal and adjusts its filtering over time (threshold calibration). The Control Plane default view shows ONLY exceptions. Autonomous workflows are invisible unless the operator drills into the fleet view. This is the 2% paradigm: of 50 active workflows, the Finance Controller sees only the 1-2 needing attention.
Key Technologies: Fleet Manager agent (intelligent filtering), Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) validator executors (deterministic threshold routing), autonomy thresholds, business impact ranking, pattern grouping, false-positive learning
POC Demo: POC1: Show 30-50 workflows running — operator sees only 2-3 exceptions. Demonstrate that the other 47 are running autonomously and invisible by default.

Question: When a human intervenes, how quickly do they get full context: what the agent was doing, why it stopped, what it tried, what it recommends, and what the options are?
Response: Target: full context within 5 seconds of clicking a workflow. The Control Plane drill-down presents a structured situational awareness view composed by the Fleet Manager: (1) What the agent was doing — workflow timeline showing completed phases, current phase, and upcoming phases. Key data points from each phase. (2) Why it stopped — the specific exception, decision point, or confidence gap that triggered the exception. (3) What it tried — OTEL trace summary showing reasoning steps, tool calls attempted, and errors encountered. Not raw traces — the Fleet Manager summarises into human-readable narrative. (4) What it recommends — the Fleet Manager's recommendation based on policy, precedents, and data analysis. Confidence level on the recommendation. (5) What the options are — approve as recommended, modify parameters and approve, reject and return to queue, escalate to another role, terminate workflow. One-click actions for common decisions. The <5 second target is achievable because the Fleet Manager pre-composes situational context as part of its continuous assessment — it doesn't compute on-demand when the operator clicks.
Key Technologies: Fleet Manager agent (pre-composed context), OTEL trace summaries, Custom Control Plane UI, workflow state store
POC Demo: POC1: Click into invoice exception — full context in <5 seconds. Show structured narrative, recommendation, and one-click action options.

Question: Can humans review and approve agent actions in bulk with configurable batch review policies and spot-check sampling?
Response: Yes. The Fleet Manager groups similar exceptions for bulk approval. Pattern grouping: (1) Same decision type — 8 interview schedules, all low-risk, all for similar roles. (2) Same risk level — batch of routine invoice approvals below the HITL threshold. (3) Same recommended action — multiple workflows where the Fleet Manager recommends the same action. Bulk approval: operator reviews the batch summary, spot-checks 1-2 items for confidence, and approves the entire batch in a single action. The Control Plane sends `raise_event` to all waiting Durable Functions instances simultaneously — each DF instance resumes its MAF workflow graph from the checkpointed state preserved via the MAF Durable Task extension. Configurable batch policies: minimum spot-check rate (e.g. review at least 2 of 8), maximum batch size, risk-level restrictions (high-risk items cannot be bulk-approved). Batch approval is logged as a single action with the batch composition and spot-check details for audit.
Key Technologies: Fleet Manager (batch composition), Custom Control Plane UI (bulk approval), Azure Durable Functions (parallel raise_event), MAF Durable Task extension (checkpointed MAF graph resumes), configurable batch policies
POC Demo: POC1: Show bulk approval — 8 similar invoices batched, operator spot-checks 2, approves all 8 in one action. All workflows resume.

Question: Does the platform provide decision-support, real-time coaching, and proactive knowledge augmentation (precedents, policies, relevant data) for human operators?
Response: Yes. Skill amplification is delivered by the Fleet Manager agent and the human's PA, grounded in the Intelligence Layer (Foundry IQ + Fabric IQ + Work IQ). When an operator faces a decision: (1) The Fleet Manager queries Foundry IQ for relevant context — policy excerpts retrieved across SharePoint, OneLake, employment-law corpora, and historical workflow archives in a single permission-aware retrieval call. (2) Fabric IQ's semantic ontology provides the business-rule context — what the WPP-specific approval thresholds are, which entities are involved, which past comparable cases exist with similar entity structure. (3) The PA can provide additional coaching on demand via Foundry IQ — the operator asks their PA for more context and receives domain-specific guidance with citations. (4) Proactive augmentation — when the operator views a workflow, the Fleet Manager highlights relevant policies and precedents without being asked. Example: HR BP reviewing a German hire compliance exception — the Fleet Manager proactively surfaces (via Foundry IQ) BetrVG works council requirements; similar past German hires from Fabric IQ's ontology graph; recommended notification template; and current works council availability via Work IQ. This transforms the operator from 'someone who approves things' into 'an expert who makes informed decisions quickly.'
Key Technologies: Fleet Manager (proactive augmentation), PA (coaching), Foundry IQ (agentic retrieval over policy + precedents), Fabric IQ (semantic graph of past cases), Work IQ (M365 context), Control Plane (contextual display)
POC Demo: POC2: Show skill amplification — HR BP reviewing compliance exception for German hire. Fleet Manager surfaces (via Foundry IQ) works council policy excerpts with citations; (via Fabric IQ) graph of similar past German hires across WPP agencies; (via Work IQ) works council representative's calendar availability; recommended action.

Question: Can the platform measure human-agent team performance: intervention rate, resolution time, override frequency, quality delta? Used to calibrate autonomy and identify training needs?
Response: Yes. Human performance analytics are derived from the action ledger and OTEL telemetry. Measurable metrics: (1) Intervention rate — percentage of workflows requiring human intervention per operator. Tracked over time to show autonomy trends. (2) Resolution time — time from exception surfacing to operator decision. Identifies bottlenecks and training needs. (3) Override frequency — how often the operator changes the agent's recommendation. High override rates indicate threshold miscalibration or skill quality issues. (4) Quality delta — outcomes of overridden decisions vs agent recommendations. Do overrides improve outcomes? Calibration: the Fleet Manager analyses these metrics and proposes autonomy threshold adjustments — if an operator never overrides screening decisions above 80% confidence, the auto-shortlist threshold can be raised from 85% to 80%. Training needs: operators with unusually high resolution times or low-confidence decisions are flagged for additional training or policy guidance.
Key Technologies: Action ledger, OTEL telemetry, Fleet Manager (performance analysis), Control Plane (analytics dashboard)
POC Demo: POC2: Show human performance analytics — intervention rates, resolution times, override patterns across the HR BP's workflow fleet.
